Hi Sarah — technical notes below (summary first, details after). Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Summary: Redwood supports three operational patterns. We recommend offering AtlasBank BYOK as preferred for regulated workloads; Redwood-managed KMS is available as an option with documented SLAs.

Patterns (brief):
- BYOK (preferred): Customer retains primary key material in their HSM. Redwood receives a wrapped/unwrapped ephemeral key for inference; we never persist the unwrapped key.
- Redwood-managed KMS: Keys stored in Redwood KMS (AES-256 keys), HSM-backed key material available on request. Rotation policy default 90 days; can be shortened contractually.
- Escrow/HSM handoff: For customers that require import/export, we can coordinate secure key handoff via PKCS#12 or KMIP export with step-by-step attestation.

Access & Audit:
- All key operations are logged to an immutable audit stream (timestamp, operator id, operation type). Logs retained 1 year by default; configurable.
- Separation of duties: key ops and platform ops are distinct roles; access requires 2-person approval for export actions.
- Key destruction: zeroization procedure documented; crypto-material destruction attested in exit report.

Constraints & proposals to capture in TOMs: concrete rotation cadence (90d default), mandatory logging + retention, 2-person approval for export, and byok flow description (including wrapped-key lifecycle).

Detailed attachment: Redwood_TOMs_KMS_Proposal.pdf — contains flow diagrams, sample audit entries, and suggested exhibit language (section A.2).

Diego Fernandez
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_TOMs_KMS_Proposal.pdf (PDF, 420KB)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@atlasbank.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA: TOMs / KMS questions + redlines attached

Sarah — thanks for the patience. I reviewed AtlasBank’s redlines and Diego’s proposal and produced a consolidated DPA with TOMs edits. Key commercial/contract notes:

- BYOK: We can accept BYOK language that makes the customer responsible for key custody and primary key rotation, with Redwood responsible for using the wrapped key for processing and for secure handling during the session. The exhibit will describe the wrap/unwrap handshake and the non-persistence guarantee.
- Redwood-managed keys: we will commit to 90-day rotation and documented destruction on termination; we will not accept an unlimited escrow liability but can offer an optional HSM escrow service as a billable add-on.
- Audit & access: Add explicit audit retention of 12 months by default; longer retention available via addendum. 2-person approval required for any key export.

I’ve attached Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf with tracked changes and a clean exhibit text in the last section (exhibit A). If AtlasBank is happy with the language, Marissa will prepare the DocuSign envelope. We typically include the DPA and TOMs exhibit as individual attachments in the envelope so both documents are bound to the signature.

We can also include a short onboarding checklist for key handoff ops to be completed before first production traffic.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf (PDF, 85KB)]
